title: Combination Sum II
statement: Candidates may contain duplicates. Return all unique combinations that sum to the target, using each candidate (each position) at most once. Combinations with the same values must not be repeated.

hints.1_question: Like Combination Sum, but each element is used once and equal values must not produce the same combination twice.
hints.2_nudge: Sort. Recurse with start = i + 1. Within one loop, skip a value that equals the previous sibling (i > start and cands[i] == cands[i-1]).
hints.3_big_hint: bt(start, rem): if rem == 0 record; for i from start: break if cands[i] > rem; skip duplicate siblings; append; bt(i+1, rem - cands[i]); pop.

known_bugs.name: no duplicate handling
known_bugs.followup: With two 1s in the input, how many times does [1, 7] appear in your answer?

known_bugs.name: allows reusing a candidate
known_bugs.followup: Each element may be used only once. After choosing index i, which index should the next call start from?

known_bugs.name: skip rule without sorting
known_bugs.followup: Your duplicate check compares neighbours. In [2, 5, 2, 1, 2] are equal values next to each other?

followups: Why must the skip check use `i > start` rather than `i > 0`?
How would counting distinct values avoid sorting?
